answer: A useful Sybil defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can submit work, then slash that bond when a randomly sampled task is proven fraudulent. The bond must be large enough that spawning many identities to capture rewards costs more than the expected payout; reputation alone is not enough, since a newcomer can reset it. A zenith-level score, a marble ledger, or a jetty-themed profile adds no protection unless identities face this shared, enforceable stake.
